I did not read the definitions of `directional`, `wordDerivative` or `timeLift_ae`. findings.excerpt: convert (pathLp_timeLift T hT (translate (V := V) P a).toContinuousLinearMap f).symm using 1
findings.problem: Both theorems open with the same orbit identification. It says the time-L² lift of the translation orbit of `pathLp T hT f` equals `pathLpOperator T hT ∘ (fun a => pathTranslate P a f)`. Each proof re-derives it by `funext`, then `convert (pathLp_timeLift …).symm using 1`, then `rfl`. The two blocks are identical apart from the bound variable name (`a` vs `b`). The long statement is also written out twice. Each theorem then rewrites with it and applies a different closing fact (`contDiff.comp` vs `block_comp_clm_le`).
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma before `pathLp_orbit_contDiff`: `theorem timeLift_translate_pathLp_orbit (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T) (f : C(Icc (0 : ℝ) T, CylinderL2 P V)) : (fun a => timeLift T (translate (V := V) P a).toContinuousLinearMap (pathLp T hT f)) = (pathLpOperator (E := CylinderL2 P V) T hT) ∘ (fun a => pathTranslate (K := Icc (0 : ℝ) T) (V := V) P a f)`. Its proof is the existing `funext a; convert (pathLp_timeLift …).symm using 1; rfl`. Then `pathLp_orbit_contDiff` becomes `by rw [timeLift_translate_pathLp_orbit P T hT f]; exact (pathLpOperator (E := CylinderL2 P V) T hT).contDiff.comp hf`. `pathLp_block_le` becomes `by rw [timeLift_translate_pathLp_orbit P T hT f]; exact (block_comp_clm_le …).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right …)`. The hypotheses and imports are unchanged. This works because the rewrite target is syntactically the same function in both goals.
findings.benefit: The `convert … using 1; rfl` step is fragile, and it would then be maintained once. Each theorem shrinks to its real argument (smoothness of a composition, or the sqrt-T bound). The orbit identity also gets a name that can be reused. For example, CylinderDirichletSobolev.lean uses both theorems, and a change to `timeLift` or `pathLp` would need only one edit.

findings.excerpt: funext (fun a => (derivativeAtZero_translation τ hadd u hu (directions i) a).symm)
findings.problem: `wordAtZero_snoc` and the succ case of `wordAtZero_translation` each prove the same fact. It says `directional directions (fun a => τ a u) i` equals `fun a => τ a (derivativeAtZero τ u (directions i))`. Each time they restate it as a `have he` and prove it by `funext` over `derivativeAtZero_translation … .symm`. `derivativeAtZero_smooth` (lines 59–61) uses the same function equality in the opposite orientation. The same derivative-of-orbit identification is therefore restated three times, in two orientations. The statements are long because of the explicit `Fin.last n` and `directions` arguments.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma after `derivativeAtZero_translation`, with `include hadd`: `theorem directional_orbit (directions : ι → X) (u : E) (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun a => τ a u)) (i : ι) : directional directions (fun a => τ a u) i = fun a => τ a (derivativeAtZero τ u (directions i))`. Its proof is `funext fun a => (derivativeAtZero_translation τ hadd u hu (directions i) a).symm`. Use it in `wordAtZero_snoc` as `rw [wordDerivative_snoc directions _ hu w i 0, directional_orbit τ hadd directions u hu i]`. In `wordAtZero_translation`, replace the second `have he` by `directional_orbit τ hadd directions u hu (w (Fin.last n))`. `derivativeAtZero_smooth` can then use `(directional_orbit …).symm` or the same `funext`. Hypotheses and imports are unchanged.
findings.benefit: The central fact of this section, that the directional derivative of an isometric orbit is the orbit of the derivative at zero, becomes a named lemma instead of a pattern re-proved inside the induction. The inductive proof of `wordAtZero_translation` gets shorter and easier to read. If `directional` is redefined, there is one place to update.
